correctness.rationale: PASS. For the d-dimensional unit l1 cross-polytope C_d and its signed coordinate vertex set V_d, the deficit H_d(t), the volume of (1+t)C_d outside V_d+tC_d, is well-defined for all integer d>=2 and real t>=0. Direct l1 geometry gives distance to nearest vertex s+1-2 min(M,1), where s=sum |x_i| and M=max |x_i|. For 0<=t<=1 the 2d translated tC_d interiors are disjoint, yielding vol(C_d)[(1+t)^d-2d t^d]. For t>=1 each orthant’s upper-bounded simplex slices reduce via exact inclusion-exclusion to the specified positive-part polynomial sum over j=3..d; it vanishes exactly for t>=d-1. Differentiating finite positive-part terms gives the stated (d-1)-derivative jump at t=1 and d-derivative jumps at integers 2..d-2, with final positive chamber coefficient. Independently evaluated 420 exact rational samples for d=2..13 against separately derived slice integrals, including boundary/threshold cases; finite checks do not replace the all-d proof.
residual_risks: Exact t and d coverage is for equally dilated l1 cross-polytopes at signed coordinate vertices only, not arbitrary vertex configurations or Euclidean balls.

The finite-convexification deficit of a vertex set plus a dilated copy of its convex hull is a standard, natural measure of how far a nonconvex Minkowski sum is from filling its hull. The exact binomial spline relates geometric overlap chambers to regularity and captures the full pre-threshold behavior that qualitative convexification criteria omit.
